ns2:section.sectionText: Full Section Title: Local Dimensions of Global Environmental Change This course examines the role of local political-ecological contexts in shaping the impacts of and responses to global environmental change. Draws on international case studies to explore themes such as urbanization and city environments, climate change, energy and natural resource management, and food systems. Explores the role of local institutions, planners, social movements, and the private sector in both creating and addressing global environmental challenges. Designed for students interested in international environmental planning, sustainable development, environmental justice, and environmental policy and management. Credit will not be given for this section of GLBL 296 (Fall 2021, CRN 54534, section LDE) if credit was given for UP 199 (Fall 2019, CRN 72448, section SK) or UP 246 (all terms, all CRNs/sections).
